title: Kamarajar and the Hungry Cowherd: 'Close the File, Feed the Child!' — 1956
summary: While stopping at a railway level-crossing in a dusty village, Chief Minister Kamaraj asked a boy grazing cattle why he was not in school. The boy replied: 'If I go to school, who will give me food?' Kamaraj immediately ordered the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, cutting through finance bureaucrats' objections with rustic wisdom.
keywords: Kamarajar and the Hungry Cowherd: 'Close the File, Feed the Child!' — 1956
full_text:
In 1955, Chief Minister K. Kamaraj's car was halted at a railway level-crossing near Cheranmahadevi in Tirunelveli district. Looking out the window, Kamaraj saw a young boy clad in torn shorts herding cattle under the blazing sun.

Kamaraj rolled down the window and called the boy over.
"Tambi, why aren't you in school at this hour?" Kamaraj asked with genuine affection.

The boy wiped his brow, looked at the tall khadi-clad leader, and answered matter-of-factly:
"If I go to school, who will give me food? If I graze these cows, the owner gives me cold rice porridge for lunch. Can your school give me that?"

The level-crossing gates opened, but the car journey was silent. Those plain words echoed relentlessly in Kamaraj's mind.

Back in Fort St. George, Chennai, Kamaraj summoned the Education Director N.D. Sundaravadivelu and the Finance Secretary.
"We must provide free lunch to every child who comes to our primary schools," Kamaraj decreed.

The Finance Secretary hesitated, nervously adjusting his ledger:
"Sir, with all due respect, our treasury is running on a deficit. Where will we find the lakhs of rupees for rice, dal, and cooking pots? The administrative rules do not permit such expenditure."

Kamaraj looked sternly at the bureaucrat:
"A hungry belly cannot learn arithmetic or science. Close your rulebooks! When British rulers needed crores for war, did they cite rules? If our children stay illiterate because of hunger, what is the point of having a treasury? Go to the public, collect rice donations, and put government funds alongside them. Close the file and feed the child!"

Thus was born the historic Free Mid-Day Meal Scheme in 1956—a revolutionary intervention that filled classrooms, eradicated child hunger, and became a national model for all of India.
